cards.explanation: The answer is Titus, friends. Paul says, "I had no peace in my spirit, because I did not find my brother Titus there." A door stood open for the gospel in Troas, and still Paul says he had no peace. I think that tells you how much Titus mattered to him.

The answer is that Paul says goodbye and goes on to Macedonia. He told the people in Troas goodbye and went on, even with a door standing open and no peace in his spirit. I think that's a man who couldn't settle with his friend missing.

The answer is the fragrance of knowing Him, friends. God "…through us spreads everywhere the fragrance of the knowledge of Him." Think about walking past a bakery. You don't need a sign, your nose already knows something good is going on in there. That's the kind of thing Paul is describing, something you can smell from a distance.

The answer is False, friends, because Paul says it covers two groups. He says they are "…the sweet aroma of Christ among those who are being saved and those who are perishing." That aroma isn't locked in one room. It goes out to both.

The word is life, friends. Paul says, "To the one we are an odor that brings death, to the other a fragrance that brings life." Same aroma going out, two different results. That's the contrast the whole verse turns on.

The answer is False, friends. Paul says, "…we are not like so many others, who peddle the word of God for profit." Instead he says, "…in Christ we speak before God with sincerity, as men sent from God." Not a salesman's pitch, just sincere speaking.

The answer is the Corinthians themselves, friends. Paul says, "You yourselves are our letter, inscribed on our hearts, known and read by everyone." The people he was writing to are the letter. That's some real mail!

The answer is the Spirit of the living God, friends. The letter is "…written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God…" No pen and no ink here. The Spirit of the living God is the One who writes it.

The word is hearts, friends. Paul says the letter is written "…not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts." Stone on one side, human hearts on the other. The letter from Christ is written on people.

The answer is True, friends. Paul writes, "Not that we are competent in ourselves to claim that anything comes from us, but our competence comes from God." It's honest. He points the credit straight at God.
The word is new, friends. Paul says God "…has qualified us as ministers of a new covenant, not of the letter but of the Spirit…" Notice who does the qualifying. It's God, not Paul.
